description.value: The study examined ACC structure and its relationships with inhibition performance in adolescents with and without heavy prenatal alcohol exposure.

spans.text: We sought to examine whether the structure of the ACC related to behavioral performance on a standardized neuropsychological measure of inhibitory control in adolescents with prenatal alcohol exposure.

value: we expected alcohol-exposed youth to demonstrate poorer inhibition completion time and inhibition error scores compared to non-exposed children
we predicted that alcohol-exposed adolescents would have reduced ACC volume compared to non-exposed controls
we predicted that alcohol-exposed adolescents would have reduced ACC area but not thickness
we expected that smaller ACCs would be associated with worse inhibition time and accuracy in both groups

description.value: A cross-sectional observational study of adolescents with and without heavy prenatal alcohol exposure.

spans.text: First, the cross sectional nature of our study prevents examination of ACC and inhibition relationships across development.

Fifty-five youth ages 12–17 years ( M = 15.0, SD = 1.3) with (AE; n = 32) and without (CON; n = 21) histories of heavy prenatal alcohol exposure participated in this study as part of a larger ongoing project at the Center for Behavioral Teratology at San Diego State University.

To examine the main effect of group three between-subjects MANCOVAs were performed on each of the following sets of dependent variables: (a) Surface Area : rrACC area, rcACC area, lrACC area, lcACC area; (b) Volume : rrACC volume, rcACC volume, lrACC volume, lrACC volume; (c) Cortical Thickness : rrACC thickness, rcACC thickness, lrACC thickness, lrACC thickness.

Written informed consent was obtained from each parent or legal guardian and assent was obtained from each subject in accordance with Institutional Review Boards at San Diego State University and University of California, San Diego.

value: For the alcohol-exposed group, a smaller right caudal ACC surface area was associated with slower inhibition completion time, whereas right caudal ACC surface area was not significantly associated with inhibition completion time in controls. The authors interpret this group difference as potentially reflecting delayed or underdeveloped ACC surface-area maturation in alcohol-exposed youth.

description.value: The inhibition subtest measured processing speed, inhibitory control, and switching.

spans.text: The inhibition subtest (IN) is comprised of three conditions: (i) the Naming condition (IN-Naming) measures speeded naming of shapes (circles and squares) and directions of arrows (up and down) and is used as a measure of processing speed; (ii) the Inhibition condition (IN-Inhibition) measures inhibitory control, the ability to inhibit the prepotent response to name the shape or direction of an arrow; and (iii) the Switching condition (IN-Switching) measures set shifting and cognitive flexibility, in combination with inhibitory control abilities, as assessed by switching between naming and inhibiting responses.

Subjects completed the NEPSY-II Inhibition subtest and the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children – fourth edition (WISC-IV; ) as a part of a neuropsychological battery administered in a larger, ongoing study.
